title: Normalization Appendix: Rosetta 67P 4-Way Ablation

ablation_results.interpretation: Cavity 5.3x higher. Standard normalization amplifies cavity signal because mean_B approaches zero.
Nearly identical to current. The 1 nT floor rarely triggers because mean_B is mostly above 1 nT even near cavity.

ablation_results.description: Bx/|B|, By/|B|, Bz/|B|, 0.0 (unit vectors, no magnitude info)
ablation_results.interpretation: Cavity 1.9x higher even with pure direction embedding. This is genuine phase-geometry disorder: field direction is highly disordered inside cavity where |B| is near noise floor. ~40% of full contrast is genuine directional phase geometry.

ablation_results.description: Bx, By, Bz, |B| (unnormalized, physical units nT)
ablation_results.interpretation: REVERSED: outside 6.9x higher. Raw associator scales with field strength. Cavity has near-zero |B| so raw associator is small. This confirms normalization is doing real work.

synthesis: The Rosetta cavity/outside contrast has three components: (1) ~40% is genuine directional phase geometry (field orientation is disordered in cavity), (2) ~60% is normalization amplification (dividing by near-zero mean_B inflates components), (3) raw embedding reverses the contrast entirely. The direction-only embedding is the cleanest test: 1.9x genuine cavity contrast survives removal of all magnitude information.
